title: R' Yaakov of Kefar Chitayya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Chagigah 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.5b) relates that Rabbi and Rabbi Chiyya came to a certain place and went to greet a Torah scholar who was blind. He blessed them, and they asked him: “From whom did you hear this?” He told them that he had heard it in a discourse of Rabbi Yaakov of Kefar Chitayya, who used to greet his teacher every day. When he (Rabbi Yaakov) grew old, he was told: “Let the master not trouble himself,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: וברכן means that the blind scholar blessed the visitors, correcting the earlier draft’s reversal. כי קש means “when he grew old,” not “when he was in distress”; Hyman explicitly inserts “R' Yaakov” in parentheses. The final speaker is not named, so “he was told” preserves the address without adding the model’s speculative “[his teacher].” מאור עינים is used euphemistically for blindness. The heading/body spellings חיטייה and חיטייא are preserved in the Hebrew source. The printed locator ה: is conventionally 5b. The full Hebrew paragraphs in the William Davidson vocalized Aramaic edition at Chagigah 5b have now been checked: רבי ורבי חייא and רבי יעקב איש כפר חיטייא support the narrative titles and the blessing/discourse context. The abbreviated heading remains R', without extending that title decision to other occurrences or identifying an unnamed speaker.
